notes.meaning: Nicodemus was an important Jewish leader and a Pharisee, a group known for strictly keeping religious laws. He was a member of the high council called the Sanhedrin, which held great authority in Israel. Even with all his learning and high status, he still needed to discover the truth about God from Jesus.

Nicodemus visited Jesus after dark, likely out of fear of what other leaders would think or to speak with Him quietly without crowds around. He called Jesus a teacher sent by God because no one could do such miraculous signs without God's power. Yet seeing Jesus merely as a good teacher was only a first step toward real faith.

Jesus cut straight to the heart of the matter by telling Nicodemus that no one can see God's kingdom without being born again. The phrase means to experience a total spiritual rebirth from above, given by God. Family heritage and good morals are not enough; our inner life must be completely remade.

Nicodemus was confused and took Jesus' words in a physical way. He asked how a grown man could enter his mother's womb a second time to be born. His reaction shows that human reasoning alone cannot grasp the spiritual work of God.

Jesus explained that entering God's kingdom requires being born of water and the Spirit. This points to the thorough cleansing of our hearts and the new spiritual life that only the Holy Spirit can give. Without this inner cleansing and renewal, no one can belong to God's family.

differ.view: Water refers either to baptism as an outward sign of the new birth or to spiritual washing, but the physical water itself does not cause rebirth.
Water refers to baptism as the outward sign and means through which the Spirit works inward renewal.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Being born of water and the Spirit refers directly to the sacrament of baptism, which washes away sin and causes spiritual rebirth.

notes.meaning: Physical birth produces physical, imperfect human life, but only the Holy Spirit can give birth to a spiritual nature. Natural human birth cannot cure our sinful condition or make us right with God. A person needs a heavenly birth to receive a new heart that loves God.

Jesus told Nicodemus not to be astonished at the statement that everyone must be born again. The need for spiritual rebirth is not just for a few bad people; it applies to all human beings, even the most religious. We should never rely on our own good works to save us.

Jesus compared the Holy Spirit to the wind, which blows wherever it pleases. You can hear the sound of the wind and see what it does, but you cannot see where it comes from or where it goes. In the same way, we cannot fully understand how the Spirit works, but we can clearly see the changed life He creates.

Nicodemus was still puzzled and asked how such a spiritual rebirth could possibly happen. He struggled to accept what he could not picture or explain with his senses. His question shows how difficult it is for human pride to accept mysteries that only God can perform.

Jesus gently challenged Nicodemus for being a respected teacher of Israel while failing to understand these truths. The Old Testament Scriptures had already promised that God would wash His people and give them a new heart and a new spirit. Religious leaders should know God's word well enough to recognize its central message.

Jesus declared that He and His witnesses speak with certain knowledge about what they have seen and known, yet the religious leaders refused to believe them. Jesus does not guess about divine truth; He speaks with direct, heavenly authority. Rejecting His teaching comes from a hard heart rather than a lack of clear evidence.

Jesus asked how Nicodemus could believe deeper heavenly truths if he could not even grasp things that happen here on earth, such as the new birth. Spiritual rebirth is experienced right here among people, yet it puzzled this teacher. If simple pictures from nature were hard to grasp, the deeper secrets of heaven would be completely beyond him.

No human being has ever climbed up to heaven to discover God's secrets and bring them back down. Only Jesus, the Son of Man, can reveal heaven because He came down from heaven and belongs there. We can trust His words because He alone has firsthand knowledge of the Father.

Jesus reminded Nicodemus of the time Moses set up a bronze snake on a pole so dying Israelites bitten by poisonous snakes could look at it and live. In the same way, the Son of Man had to be lifted up on the cross. His death was part of God's plan to save dying sinners.

Jesus explained that the purpose of His being lifted up is so that anyone who trusts in Him can receive eternal life. Just as the sick Israelites were healed simply by looking at the bronze snake, anyone who looks to Jesus in faith is rescued from death. Eternal life means sharing in God's own everlasting life beginning right now.

God loved the world so deeply that He gave His unique Son to die for human beings. The purpose of this gift is that no one who trusts in Jesus will perish, but instead will have everlasting life. This shows that the true starting point of our salvation is God's free and generous love.

differ.view: God's love is extended to every single human being in the world, and Christ was given so that anyone who chooses to believe can be saved.
The word world highlights the surprising breadth and greatness of God's love beyond Israel to all kinds of people, guaranteeing salvation for all who believe.

notes.meaning: God did not send His Son into the world to act as a judge and bring destruction on mankind. Instead, His main purpose was to rescue and save people through Him. While final judgment will come one day, Jesus' earthly mission was purely an offer of rescue and mercy.

Anyone who puts their trust in Jesus is free from condemnation, because their penalty has been paid. But those who refuse to believe are already under judgment because they reject God's only Son. A person remains condemned simply by choosing to turn away from the only Savior who can deliver them.

The verdict against unbelievers is that Jesus, the true Light, came into the world, but people preferred the dark. They chose darkness because they loved their sinful habits and did not want to give them up. People are condemned not because there was no hope, but because they deliberately hid from the truth.

People who practice wicked things hate the light because it shines on their sins and exposes their guilt. Just as criminals work under cover of night, sinners avoid God's truth to keep from feeling shame and conviction. Guilt makes people run away from God rather than seeking His pardon.

Those who love what is true and right gladly come to the light so everyone can see that their actions are done with God's help. Sincere believers have nothing to hide and want God to examine their hearts. Walking in the light brings freedom and peace because God is the source of all that is good in our lives.

After His talk with Nicodemus in Jerusalem, Jesus went out into the countryside of Judea with His followers. He spent unhurried time with them there, teaching the crowds while His disciples baptized new believers. This was a quiet, fruitful season of ministry in the rural districts.

At the same time, John the Baptist was also baptizing people at a place called Aenon near Salim, where there were plenty of springs and streams. Large crowds kept travelling there to confess their sins and be washed. John remained faithful to the work God had given him to do.

This brief note explains that these events happened before King Herod had John arrested and thrown into prison. John and Jesus were working near each other for a short season during this early stage. John kept serving God diligently until his freedom was taken away.

A disagreement broke out between some of John's disciples and a Jewish man about ceremonial washing and purifying rites. They were arguing over which baptism was better or more effective for cleansing a person before God. Arguments over religious ceremonies can easily distract believers from the main message of the gospel.

John's disciples came to him upset and jealous because Jesus was baptizing and drawing larger crowds than John was. They reminded John that he had previously spoken well of Jesus, as if Jesus now owed him loyalty. They were worried that their master was losing his fame and influence.

John answered them calmly by saying that no one can receive any true spiritual role or success unless God gives it from heaven. He knew that his own work came from God, and that Jesus' growing popularity was also planned by the Father. True servants of God do not get jealous when God blesses someone else's ministry.

John reminded his followers that he had always been open about his limited role, clearly stating that he was not the Messiah. He was only the forerunner sent ahead to prepare the road for the true King. Therefore, they should not be surprised or troubled to see people following Jesus instead of him.

John used the picture of a wedding, explaining that the bride belongs to the bridegroom, while the best man is just happy to stand nearby and listen for the groom's voice. The people belonged to Jesus, the true Bridegroom of the church, not to John. Hearing that people were turning to Jesus brought John complete and overflowing joy.

John stated clearly that Jesus must grow in honor and importance, while he himself had to become less important. Just as the morning star fades away when the sun rises, John was happy to step aside now that the Savior had arrived. True humility means gladly letting Christ receive all the praise.

Jesus came from heaven and is far greater than anyone else, holding supreme authority over all creation. Earthly teachers have their origin in this world and can only speak with limited, human understanding. Because Christ comes directly from above, His authority and message stand higher than any human leader.

Jesus speaks directly of what He has personally seen and heard with the Father in heaven, yet very few people truly welcome His message. Even though large crowds gathered around Him, few trusted Him with true, saving faith. It is heartbreaking when people turn away from divine truth that is so plainly offered.

Anyone who truly accepts what Jesus says puts their seal of approval on the fact that God is entirely truthful. In ancient times, pressing a seal into wax showed that a document was official and trustworthy. Believing in Jesus honors God by confirming that His promises are true.

The One whom God sent speaks God's exact words because the Father gives Him the Holy Spirit without any limit. Earlier prophets received gifts of the Spirit in measured amounts for special tasks, but Jesus possessed the Spirit's full power constantly. This guarantees that everything Jesus taught is the pure truth of God.

God the Father loves the Son with a special, eternal love and has placed the authority over everything into His hands. Because Christ has full control over all things, He has complete power to rule, save, and give eternal life. We can safely trust our lives to the One who holds the universe in His care.

Anyone who puts their trust in the Son possesses eternal life right now. But anyone who rejects the Son will never see life, and God's holy wrath remains on them instead. Our eternal future depends entirely on whether we welcome or reject Jesus Christ.
